messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary v3.1.0-canary crossed p95 latency threshold (baseline 120ms -> 320ms). Auto-rollback policy: wait 5m for stabilization, then shift 80% traffic to previous stable if no improvement. tagging: #canary | runbook: /runbooks/canary-rollback.md
laura: seeing this on the console. any obvious cause in the last deploy?
josh: looking at infra metrics now. early signal looks like KV cache misses spiking on specific host pool (eu-west-1-gpu-2). not global yet.
laura: ok. deploy-bot says auto will run in ~4m unless we ack. can we try a targeted pin first?
nina: product impact: a few paying customers on canary experiments, want minimal disruption. if shift is partial that's fine.
marco: oncall here. I can run a targeted traffic-split rollback for canary to 10% and monitor. prefer manual so we control customer-facing comms.
laura: agree manual. josh, can we identify the host group and drain?
josh: yes — hosts eu-west-1-gpu-2a,b show KVM miss surge. I'll cordon those instances and restart the kvcache service. steps in a sec.
ciara: Customer success wants a short note for impacted beta customers. If we do manual rollback, can we give ETA?
laura: plan: (1) ack deploy-bot to cancel auto-rollback, (2) shift canary -> 10% non-affected infra, (3) cordon/restart problematic hosts, (4) if p95 stays >200ms after 10m then full rollback to v3.0.4 stable, (5) send customer note.
laura: @deploy-bot cancel-auto-rollback (manual override) :white_check_mark:
josh: running traffic-split command now:
```
# traffic-split tool
rictl traffic split --service=inference-api --from=canary:v3.1.0-canary --to=stable:v3.0.4 --percentage=90
```
marco: shifting 90% to stable now. watching traces and traces-per-host.
josh: cordoning hosts eu-west-1-gpu-2a,b and restarting kvcache:
```
rictl host cordon eu-west-1-gpu-2a
ssh gpu-host 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-kvcache'
```
laura: good. who will draft the customer note? short, transparent. ciara you?
ciara: will draft 1-liner and share in a minute. suggested: "We observed increased latency in a canary release and have moved traffic back to the previous stable release while we investigate. No data loss."
laura: sounds good. josh please confirm p95 and error rates after traffic shift. set alert if p95 >200ms for 10m.
josh: initial after-shift p95 = 145ms, error rate steady. creating alert rule now.
marco: monitoring for 12m window. if regression returns, we escalate to full rollback.
laura: update for release notes / changelog: add 'rolled back v3.1.0-canary due to KV cache regression on select hosts; investigating root cause'.
ciara: customer note ready: "Heads up — we temporarily rolled back a canary deployment due to higher than expected latency for some beta users. Traffic has been moved back to the previous stable release while we investigate. Expect normal service; we'll follow up with details." posting to customers now.
nina: product OK with manual rollback and comms. prioritize root cause so we can re-roll with fix.
josh: logs show a recent kernel upgrade on that host group at 03:12 UTC, file a retro task and tag infra. creating ticket INF-4729.
laura: thanks team. follow-ups: josh to triage INF-4729, marco to keep watch for 1h, ciara to send follow-up to affected customers after RCA. I'll close the thread once RCA ticket has owner. :thumbsup:
